A growth team's log records four signup cohorts that received the same onboarding email.

items.confound_note: All four cohorts are starter signups in Norway inside the same March window, so one product change covers every case at once. The free trial was lengthened from seven to thirty days on 1 March, while each cohort is compared against itself in February, when the seven-day trial still applied. A thirty-day trial leaves users still inside their trial at week two, which raises week-two retention by itself, so nothing in the evidence separates the email from the trial change.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Confirm the trial extension works as a single confound ONLY because the four cohorts share tier, country, month and channel - one 1 March policy change reaches all of them, and the February baseline predates it.

items.passage:
A growth team's log records four signup cohorts that received the same onboarding email.
One: starter signups from Norway via webinar were emailed 24 March; by 9 March week-two retention ran 5 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Two: premium signups from Chile via marketplace were emailed 3 July; by 27 July week-two retention ran 3 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Three: enterprise signups from Vietnam via reseller were emailed 25 October; by 10 October week-two retention ran 6 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Four: basic signups from Ireland via podcast were emailed 2 December; by 26 December week-two retention ran 4 points above the same cohort a month earlier.
Signup volume, in-app prompts and trial length were unchanged across both periods for every cohort, and no other lifecycle message shipped.
items.confound_note: In cases one and three the retention figure was read before the email was sent: 9 March precedes 24 March, and 10 October precedes 25 October. Half the evidence therefore describes week-two retention that was already recorded when the onboarding email went out, so it cannot be evidence for that email. Cases two and four are correctly ordered but are not enough on their own.
items.notes: The closing sentence is reused VERBATIM from both TRUE items - the flaw lives entirely in the dates of cases one and three, so the unigram/bigram profile is unchanged. Check that the reversed dates stay inside their own month so the month dimension still holds four distinct values. A shared confound is unavailable here: four tiers, four countries, four channels and four months share no single event.
